Entity Access Behaviors

Entity Access Behaviors provide deterministic mechanisms for retrieving entities by identifier from FeatureCell state. These behaviors extend the FeatureCell runtime surface with entity-focused access patterns while preserving the FeatureCell pipeline as the single authoritative source of truth.

Entity access operates after state finalization and relies on committed state emissions as the authoritative data source. Each behavior exposes a different resolution model depending on how entities should be retrieved and whether additional resolution work is permitted.

Entity access behaviors do not mutate state directly and do not bypass the FeatureCell pipeline. Instead, they coordinate with the pipeline lifecycle to ensure that entity resolution remains deterministic, lifecycle-aware, and consistent with FeatureCell state semantics.

Supported entity access behaviors include:

  • Query Behavior — synchronous access to entities already present in finalized state
  • Lookup Behavior — identifier-based entity resolution through pipeline execution
  • State Cache Behavior — TTL-based entity caching with controlled refresh

Each behavior provides a different access model while maintaining a consistent integration boundary with the FeatureCell pipeline.

Entity Access Extension

Entity access behaviors extend the FeatureCell runtime with APIs that resolve entities by identifier. These APIs allow application code to retrieve entities without directly interacting with the underlying pipeline resolution mechanisms.

Entity access behaviors share several architectural guarantees:

  • They operate after pipeline finalization
  • They do not mutate FeatureCell state directly
  • They do not bypass pipeline resolution
  • They preserve FeatureCell lifecycle boundaries
  • They treat the FeatureCell state pipeline as the authoritative source of truth

Depending on the selected behavior, entity access may:

  • Resolve immediately from finalized state
  • Trigger pipeline resolution for missing entities
  • Cache resolved entities with expiration semantics

Each behavior is installed through the FeatureCell fluent configuration API during initialization.

Diagrams
Available Entity Access Behaviors

Entity access behaviors are add-on behaviors and must be registered with the during FeatureCell declaration.

These behaviors extend the FeatureCell runtime with identifier-based entity access while preserving the FeatureCell pipeline as the authoritative source of truth. Entity access operations never mutate state directly and never bypass pipeline execution.

Instead, entity access behaviors coordinate with finalized state emissions and pipeline lifecycle events to provide deterministic entity resolution.

Entity Access Behavior Models

The following table summarizes the different entity access behaviors and how they interact with FeatureCell state and pipeline execution.

Entity Access Behavior Comparison
Behavior Resolution Model Pipeline Execution Data Source Typical Use Cases
Query Behavior Immediate (synchronous) Never Finalized FeatureCell state Fast entity access when state is already populated
Lookup Behavior On-demand resolution Yes (on miss) Finalized state or pipeline fetch Lazy loading entities by identifier
State Cache Behavior TTL-based caching Yes (on miss or expiration) Cached entities derived from finalized state High-performance entity access with refresh control
Architectural Summary

Entity Access Behaviors provide structured access to entities without compromising the FeatureCell pipeline as the authoritative state mechanism.

Each behavior maintains strict alignment with pipeline semantics:

  • Query Behavior reflects finalized state.
  • Lookup Behavior resolves entities through pipeline execution.
  • State Cache Behavior augments lookup resolution with TTL-based caching.

Together, these behaviors allow FeatureCells to expose flexible entity access models while preserving deterministic state management and lifecycle control.
